title: What if I just move into the Greenwich House theater this summer?? #m...
transcript: I genuinely feel like I manifested this literally last week. Someone asked me what theatre I was most excited about in New York this summer, and I had like two shows, but I said, honestly, it's a pretty quiet summer. There's not much happening. Then Matchbook Fest announced, and suddenly the rest of my summer is booked. Matchbook Fest is a brand new festival taking over the Greenwich House Theatre from July 22nd to August 21st. It's bringing together plays, concerts, comedy, conversations, cabarets, one person shows, and new work at every stage of development. So basically, this is extremely my thing. The whole schedule looks amazing, and there are still things are going to announce, but here are a few that I am particularly excited about. I don't know about you, but Theater Talk on Channel 13 was a critical part of my Broadway education. I loved this show As a kid it was just interviews with actors and composers and directors. Michael and Patrick are kicking off the festival on July 22nd with a reunion conversation. I'm just really curious what they have to say cause a lot has changed since they were on the air and since Theater Talk started. I bought a ticket to this the second it dropped. Steady is a new play written by Trey Everett, who wrote obit, which is a play I loved and has new music by Eleri Ward. One of my faves. It's directed and choreographed by the Ellenore Scott and stars Damon Dannou And Sammie Williams. I didn't even look up the plot, but it's about a world renowned dance company artistic manager and his toxic relationship with his up and coming star. So it sounds great. And then this is my second Cannot miss Matt Doyle and Bonnie Milligan. Mentally unwell, but funny. Literally two of my favorite performers, two of my favorite singers, two of my favorite all time Tony winners. It's a cabaret. I don't know what it is. I frankly don't care. I will be there. if You loved Blues Clues. This is Steve the Steve and I loved Blues Clues, so this is his one man show about fame and grief and internet mythology. I'm super intrigued by Rosie the musical cause this is very early in its developmental process. It's about Rosie the Riveter, you know, with the blue shirt and like the red Bandana that that poster and you know, like I love Suffs. So I feel like it's in that kind of vein but supposed to be very funny. This is a great way to see a workshop of a new show. And then unfortunately I leave the city August 9th through the rest of the festival. But there are a few things that like you need to go to For me first is the Joe Iconis musical hootenanny. Because everything Joe Iconis is always going to be a ride. It promises quote “various assorted creatures who populate the nooks and crannies of the New York theater scene.” I'm sad I won't be there. And lastly, Zach Zadek and friends who is a musical theatre writer who I really like. I went to a concert for one of his shows a few months ago. I was blown away by the music and the talent. You should go. I'm barely scratching the surface of events with Alex Lippa and Bryce Pinkham and Alex Moffat. You can buy tickets for the entire line up on TodayTix right now. And let me know what you're going to see cause there is so much.
